newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn coalition, SPD agree to meet again on tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Bonn coalition, SPD agree to meet again on tax cuts.

text.p: The German government and opposition Social Democrats (SPD) agreed to meet again on March 8 in an attempt to hammer out differences on tax reform, SPD leaders said on Friday after a second top-level summit.

"It would still be sensible to meet again on March 8 to overcome our deep-seated differences of opinion," said SPD parliamentary faction leader Rudolf Scharping. The main problems remain on cuts in income taxes and relief on late shifts, he said.
Scharping said the SPD considered a cut in labour overheads -- which includes unemployment insurance cuts -- in mid-1997 to be the best way to boost the jobs market.

Before the talks, which followed an opening round on Monday, the two sides said there was room to compromise on the most controversial issue of planned sweeping tax reforms -- top-rate income tax cuts to 39 from 53 percent.
Negotiators from the two sides sought a quick compromise on passing tax reforms to battle unemployment which climbed in January to 4.7 million -- the highest since 1933.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition wants a deal by Easter, and failure would condemn the measures to long wrangling in parliament, where the SPD can block tax changes through its majority in the upper house of parliament.
